chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Jamilah from Aban ibn Taghlib from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding
a woman died and left behind her parents and her husband. He (peace be upon him) said: 'For the husband is half, and for the mother is one-sixth, and for the father is what remains.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This is a report consistent with the general public (Sunni scholars), but we do not act upon it because of the consensus of the Righteous Faction on abandoning acting upon it, and because of its contradiction to the apparent meaning of the Quran and the mutawatir (concurrently transmitted) reports. Allah the Exalted said: 'If he has no child and his parents inherit him, then for his mother is one-third.' Thus, He obligated for her, in the absence of a child, one-third in its entirety. So whoever reduces her from that is contradicting the apparent meaning of the Book. And even if the report were safe from that, it would be permissible to be interpreted as being when there are siblings who restrict the mother from one-third to one-sixth, for we have clarified that in the first chapter, and it is consistent with the apparent meaning of the Book. Allah the Exalted said: 'If he has siblings, then for his mother is one-sixth.' And in the report is not mentioned that there was no one among the brothers or sisters who would restrict [her share].

key_terms.الثُّلُثُ: One-third (share of the mother in absence of children/siblings)
key_terms.السُّدُسُ: One-sixth (share of the mother in presence of siblings)
key_terms.الطَّائِفَةُ الْمُحِقَّةُ: The Righteous Faction (a key Shia scholarly group)
key_terms.يَحْجُبُونَ: Restrict/Reduce (referring to the effect of siblings on the mother's share)

ai.seo_question: How do Shia scholars reconcile the inheritance of the mother when there are no children but there are siblings?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to illustrate the Shia rejection of the 'half for husband, one-sixth for mother' distribution, arguing it contradicts the explicit Quranic mandate of one-third for the mother in the absence of descendants. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan clarifies that the report is likely restricted to cases where siblings exist to reduce the mother's share, thereby aligning it with the Quranic verse 4:11, or it stands as a distinct view opposed by the consensus of the 'True Sect'.
